162	
163	One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
164	`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).
165	
166	- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
167	  ineligible after 4 s.
168	- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
169	  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
170	- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
171	  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
172	- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
173	- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
174	  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
175	  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
176	- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
177	  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
178	- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
179	  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
180	- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
181	  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
182	- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
183	  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Verify TAN signing with test runs, which get fresh logins (up to 5 per team at
184	  once, 3 more waiting); see the isolation probe below for what else is shared.
185	- Isolation probe (two browser contexts, scouting login): the bid wizard's progress lives in the session cookie, not
186	  the account (A advanced to step 2, a fresh context B still saw an empty step 1), so local bid-form runs do not see
187	  each other's wizard. The webmail is one shared mailbox (same list in both contexts, TAN mails numbered across all
188	  teams), so TAN requests remain the only collision: stop local runs before the TAN request, sign in test runs.
189	- Scouting logins are shared by all teams: TAN request numbers are global and a request from another team
190	  invalidates ours (local runs saw "Anforderung 59" rejected after someone requested 60). The bid wizard state is
191	  per browser session, so local runs are fine for the form phase; measure signing only in test runs
192	  (`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN=1` stops a local run before the TAN request).
193	- Bid speed-up, test runs: baseline 201 s; two phases (form thinking off, review thinking on) 271 s (one run:
194	  documents detour, mail lookup hit its step limit, slow thinking steps); review thinking off too 171 s;
195	  final variant 94, 96, 105 and 87 s (4 runs), quality 10 each, cost $0.008 to $0.010 instead of $0.019.
196	- Final variant: form phase thinking off with fill_in() (several form actions per step), then one thinking-off
197	  model call checks the review page, then the signing phase (thinking off unless the check fails or finds
198	  problems) uses request_signing_tan(ref), which clicks the model-chosen button and fetches the TAN in one tool.

202	- Thinking-off form steps sometimes click the wrong ref on the one-position-per-step configurator ("add

210	  view, so after any note() the model had no page at all and invented values (refused notes, re-opened pages). Now
211	  the latest view stays until a newer one arrives, and the first prompt's view is trimmed once superseded.
212	- Same-page actions now return only the changed parts (controls are separate pieces, unchanged refs stay valid) or
213	  "unchanged"; the full view stays in context and in the cached prefix. Invented form (fill, select, tick, save):
214	  ~27.7k -> ~20.6k input tokens, correct in 7/7 runs. Read-only sites navigate, so diffs rarely fire there.

# CLAUDE.md

Team error404.ai at the Atira EHL Challenge ("From RFQ to bid", challenge id `rfq`, event 10 Oct 2026, up to 5 people
per team). The agent lives in `agent/` and is built on the Atira starter kit. Keep the GitHub repo private.

## Status and layout

- `docs/plan.md`: framework decision (pydantic-ai on Qwen, no LangGraph, no browser-agent framework), module layout,
  site scouting notes and the roadmap v0 to v5. Read it first. Its scouting notes describe public-1 only: they inform
  generic helpers, they must never become hardcoded paths, labels, values or prompt text (the private final run uses
  other software, layouts and data).
- `agent/`: starter kit (`run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py`) plus the harness (`llm.py`, `extract.py`,
  `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `tracing.py`) and v1: `agent.py` `solve()` reads the brief (`briefing.py`), then
  `submit.py` signs a bid with every position omitted, fetching the contact address and TAN from the webmail.
  `calc.py` holds the deterministic bid rules (tested, not wired in yet). `agent.json` asks for 2 browsers.
- `dev/smoke.py`: the v0 check (one worker per site logs in and reads a page). From the repo root:
  `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/smoke.py [siteId ...]`
- Next: v2 to v4 for field points (research workers for spec, ERP, tender Q&A and mail, wired into `calc.py`). Use
  `git status` and `atira status` for the current state; do not trust dated numbers in this file.

## Tracking runs

Record every test run and submission; they go to `experiments/runs.jsonl` (append-only, `merge=union`, committed with
the change it measured). Local runs go to `experiments/local-runs.jsonl` (gitignored). `python3 dev/track.py report`
renders both to `docs/experiments.md` (gitignored). From the repo root:

```sh
dev/test-run.sh v1 "what changed" [experiment]    # sandbox test run, followed to the end, score recorded
dev/run-local.sh v1 "what changed" [experiment]   # local, headless; needs `atira models proxy`
python3 dev/track.py platform <sub_id> --version v1 --experiment NAME --note "..."   # after `atira submit`
```

`version` is the base being measured (v1, v2, ...); `experiment` names what a run varies on top of it (e.g.
`thinking-off-forms`, `model-<name>`, `4-browsers`), so variants of one version compare side by side. Environment
overrides (`AGENT_*`, `LLM_*`, `THINKING*`, `MAX_STEPS*`) are recorded, with secrets redacted. `atira test-run`
uploads untracked files too, so the recorded commit is a pointer; `atira package <id>` shows the exact upload.
When a run taught something (a failure mode, a speed-up, a score change), add a bullet to `docs/learned.md`. Notes
never contain credentials or values copied from the sites.

## Platform docs (source of truth; re-read, they change)

Base `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai`. Public pages (home, start, challenge, leaderboard, team profiles) are also
Markdown via `.md`; docs are `/docs/<name>.md`.

- `/start.md`, `/challenges/rfq.md` (29 bid rules, answer schema), `/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md`
- `/docs/fair-play.md`, `scoring.md`, `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `building-an-agent.md`, `cli.md`, `api.md`,
  `mcp.md`, `faq.md`, `demo-day.md`; `/openapi.json`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` (all docs in one file)
- Announcements need a token: `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/v1/announcements`
- Submission deadline and prizes are not in the docs: ask the organizers. Demo day: best teams run live on stage, so
  keep a one-line start command (`atira test-run ./agent`) and a fallback recording.

The scouting logins are deliberately NOT stored here: run `atira scout`. Never write them, or anything copied from
the sites, into code, prompts, fixtures, notes or fallbacks.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer rejects or flags these)

- No hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), not even as defaults,
  fallbacks or in prompts. Facts the brief states for every scenario (e.g. the sales director's mailbox) are fine.
- No pre-solving, by you or an AI assistant, put into the package. Hand-derived expectations stay outside `agent/`.
- Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path (model
  unused or only a fallback), or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation.
  Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate,
  validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers are fine.
- Only the platform API, the four sites and the model proxy; no local models; no own browsers in the sandbox (use the
  provided 1 to 4, tabs and contexts are free).
- Do not write notes meant to steer the reviewer. Outcomes: passed; flagged (runs, but hidden from the leaderboard
  until an organizer passes it); rejected (no runs).

## The task and its traps

One signed bid, entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. Site ids are
public-1 names; the private set renames and re-splits sites, so never branch code on siteId, URL or layout.

| Site | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (the hub: quantity changes, withdrawals, scoped spec amendments, Konditionsgruppe, packaging, commitment and setup-pool keys), configurator |
| Supplier portal | Buyer's spec and revisions (oldest shown first; use the one marked current) |
| ERP | Materials and status, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity and scales, pieces per carton, allocation mass |
| Webmail | Director's discount approval, TAN, authority mails (look-alikes, superseded, archive) |

Read all 29 rules in `challenges/rfq.md` before writing prompts or tools. Highest-impact traps:

- **Authority and time (21):** per key, the latest record dated no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender
  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).
- **Sign and submit:** saving alone scores nothing. Partial bids use "Position auslassen" and are still signed.
- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).
  Breakdown fields are reports, not inputs. Bonus split: largest remainders (26); setup pool: the cent-allocation rule
  stated in the Ruestpools mail (25).
- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.
- Setup has network and 5 min (untimed), but no run variables or secrets, and nothing it starts survives. The timed run
  reaches only the platform, sites and model proxy (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, honour it in custom clients). Send your own
  User-Agent (default Python agents get 403 "Error 1010").
- `agent.json`: `setup`, `run`, `models` (list every hosted model used, e.g. `["qwen","clef"]`), `browsers` 1 to 4.
  Package: 20 MB compressed and uncompressed, 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, `.gitignore` honoured, no secrets inside.
  Own model keys are team secrets (names: capitals, digits, underscore, letter first, max 20, no platform names).
- Order: eligible (right tender reference), then quality 0 to 100, then lower cost x time (floors $0.01, 1 s). A wrong
  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.
- Winners: private-dataset final run of our LATEST submission that PASSED review (not the best), then public
  leaderboard, then elegance. So: never tune to public-1; every passing `atira submit` replaces the final candidate,
  even a worse one, so confirm with the team first. `atira final --best-of 3` (before the final starts) allows three
  attempts (own-key cost up to 3x); private runs show no score breakdown.
- Models: hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`QWEN_BASE_URL/KEY`, 32 concurrent) and Clef (`CLEF_*`, 16 concurrent) are free
  but add a SIMULATED price to run cost; own-key calls are metered at provider prices through the proxy. Measured
  Qwen behaviour (thinking flag, schema cold start, caching) is in `docs/plan.md`.

## Dev loop

```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh    # CLI; the installer provides Node 24 if missing
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && atira login           # `atira upgrade` if a command is unknown
(cd agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium)
atira models proxy                       # terminal 1 (port 8765)
eval "$(atira scout --env)"              # terminal 2: scouting logins + model vars
(cd agent && uv run --no-sync python agent.py)   # local run, nothing submitted
(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)
atira test-run ./agent --dry-run         # what would upload
atira test-run ./agent --follow          # sandbox run with score breakdown
```

Debugging: `atira logs <run> --follow`, `atira status [id]`, `atira package <id> --out dir`, `atira cancel <run>`; every
command takes `--json`. `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` gives `diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`,
`run_screenshot`, `compare_runs` and more (`mcp.md`). Use the score breakdown to localise errors (zero surcharge
points can come from mass surcharge, setup or metal index inputs). A cancelled scored run ends its submission (ignored
by the leaderboard), so you may resubmit. Missing "OpenAI key" 401s mean no provider key arrived (team secret).
On macOS, python.org Python needs `Install Certificates.command` or `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

## Team conventions

- Git: commit author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`; imperative subject of at most 50 characters, body as short `-`
  bullets; no attribution trailers (no Co-Authored-By, no session links); never stage anything under `.claude/`;
  never push or open a PR without asking first.
- Never put real credentials, personal data or site values in tests, fixtures, docs or comments; invent placeholders.

# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Verify TAN signing with test runs, which get fresh logins (up to 5 per team at
  once, 3 more waiting); see the isolation probe below for what else is shared.
- Isolation probe (two browser contexts, scouting login): the bid wizard's progress lives in the session cookie, not
  the account (A advanced to step 2, a fresh context B still saw an empty step 1), so local bid-form runs do not see
  each other's wizard. The webmail is one shared mailbox (same list in both contexts, TAN mails numbered across all
  teams), so TAN requests remain the only collision: stop local runs before the TAN request, sign in test runs.
- Scouting logins are shared by all teams: TAN request numbers are global and a request from another team
  invalidates ours (local runs saw "Anforderung 59" rejected after someone requested 60). The bid wizard state is
  per browser session, so local runs are fine for the form phase; measure signing only in test runs
  (`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN=1` stops a local run before the TAN request).
- Bid speed-up, test runs: baseline 201 s; two phases (form thinking off, review thinking on) 271 s (one run:
  documents detour, mail lookup hit its step limit, slow thinking steps); review thinking off too 171 s;
  final variant 94, 96, 105 and 87 s (4 runs), quality 10 each, cost $0.008 to $0.010 instead of $0.019.
- Final variant: form phase thinking off with fill_in() (several form actions per step), then one thinking-off
  model call checks the review page, then the signing phase (thinking off unless the check fails or finds
  problems) uses request_signing_tan(ref), which clicks the model-chosen button and fetches the TAN in one tool.
- Summary check offline test (6 doctored review pages: ok, alternative offer, 5 % discount, position not
  omitted, extra position, transposed VAT id): thinking off 6/6 in 2 to 5 s, thinking on 6/6 in 4 to 27 s.
- Briefing with thinking off is correct (validated against the brief) and takes 6 to 10 s instead of 17 to 45 s.
- Thinking-off form steps sometimes click the wrong ref on the one-position-per-step configurator ("add
  position" instead of "next"); the summary check and the goal's "never use options that add positions" catch it.
- Goal wording costs time: "acknowledge the tender documents" sent the model to read every document (35 s);
  "tick the form's acknowledgement (no need to open them)" fixed it.
- After the bid is in, the platform closes the run's model token; the final model call gets 401. Caught now.
- Faster v1 submission (thinking by phase, fill_in, TAN hand-off): quality 10 in 2:34 min for $0.011, against 4:41 and
  $0.024 for the first v1; no quality loss, cost x time about 4x better.
- Page views, read-only bench (smoke goals, 3 runs each, base vs new): the history trim kept only the newest request's
  view, so after any note() the model had no page at all and invented values (refused notes, re-opened pages). Now
  the latest view stays until a newer one arrives, and the first prompt's view is trimmed once superseded.
- Same-page actions now return only the changed parts (controls are separate pieces, unchanged refs stay valid) or
  "unchanged"; the full view stays in context and in the cached prefix. Invented form (fill, select, tick, save):
  ~27.7k -> ~20.6k input tokens, correct in 7/7 runs. Read-only sites navigate, so diffs rarely fire there.
- Select lists over 600 characters show count, first 8 and last 2; `options(ref, contains)` searches them and a
  failed `select` names close matches. Costs one request when the model wants the list, saves tokens per view.
- Request makeup (smoke): system + tools ~5k chars fixed, history ~3k, view ~1.5-2.5k; 40-55 % of input is reported
  as cached, so per-request token cuts are modest; the step count dominates tokens and seconds (browser actions
  take 0.3-0.7 s, a model step 1-4 s). Repeated boilerplate lines (footer, title bar) were 1-4 % of view text when
  restricted to safe lines: not worth the risk of hiding status lines, dropped.
- Clef vs Qwen offline eval (`dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md`, 68 hand-labelled decisions from real page views, 3
  repeats): Clef answers in ~1 s and is deterministic, but loses to Qwen at picking links (79 % vs 93 % thinking
  off) and at judging the right record (88 % vs 98 % thinking on; it takes `<ref>-A` look-alikes for the exact
  reference and misses ordering such as "highest request number"). It is exact at "is this an error, empty, locked
  or decoy page after my action" (100 % vs 93 % for Qwen off, same speed). Kept only that check, behind
  `AGENT_CLEF=1` (`page_check` tool); Clef's `score` criteria must be a list, and many `noul` questions fit one call.
- Site tools (`site_tools.py` search / collect / extract), local read-only check against the scouting sites: an ERP
  search that the site refuses as too broad took 10 steps, 46 s and 34k input tokens with the tools (remark reported
  right) against 30 steps, 153 s, 112k and no answer without; a mailbox search over inbox and archive took 18 steps
  and 105 s with the tools (10 messages over 3 pages each, newest right), plain stopped at 30 steps or hung on
  re-locking gates. Two fixes were needed: older tool results were cut to one line once a newer view came, so the
  model paged again by hand to see the list it had collected (results of search / collect / extract now stay), and
  after paging the next view must come whole, not as a diff against a page the model never saw.
- v2 position filling (`configurator.py`, `PositionDesk` in `submit.py`): the model names the position on screen,
  maps control labels to value names once and names the confirm button; the helper walks the cascading selects
  one level per round trip, matches options by value (text-sorted lists, neighbouring numbers or a catalogue
  number that is a prefix of another) and formats German numbers. Offline mock and live (scouting, up to the TAN
  page): one position entered in full, a position with an impossible attribute failed and was omitted, net total
  from the entered positions only, Hauptangebot, AGB unticked; 202 s, 28 requests, 183k input tokens.
- The worker forgot the page after a note(): `_forget_old_views` kept only the last request, so a short tool
  result wiped the newest view and Qwen clicked guessed refs (hit "add position" in the mock). Keep the newest view
  in full whatever comes after it.
- Attribute wording can differ from the option text (a "none" attribute vs a "without ..." option): the tool
  reports the options and the model passes `choices`, used only when no option matches literally (an always-on
  override broke a later position that was already right).
- Without "every value is already calculated; do not research" the bid worker wandered into documents and the Q&A
  and burned its 76 steps picking options itself. The goal now says so up front.
- Phased flow (form phase thinking off) on the offline mock: positions, discount, net total, offer type and
  declarations right, summary check matched, signed in 93 s and 16 requests. Thinking-off slips seen there and
  live: the model typed its own net total (now stated in the goal), clicked "omit" on a position without asking
  configure_position() (goal: call it first on every position page), sent a partial `fields` map that replaced
  the first one and let an unrelated position count as entered (maps now merge; a position counts only with
  material, quantity, price and lead time mapped), and "chose" a neighbouring bore for an impossible one via
  `choices` (numbers must now match exactly; `choices` only for worded attributes, remembered per position).
- Live on the shared scouting login, a re-login mid-run reset the wizard to its first step; the worker re-entered
  the form from the start. Another reason to verify signing only in test runs.
- Live, thinking off, the model still entered its own "all positions" net total after one position failed and
  clicked "omit" instead of "next" right after a successful fill (that position was lost). Now every
  configure_position() result states the running net total of the positions entered, and the tool saves the
  position with the next button the model named once. Mock after that: signed and fully correct in 64 s,
  13 requests.
- Local live runs twice hung before the briefing finished: one site's start (the webmail) never returned while the
  sites answered curl at once. solve() gathers every site start without a timeout; worth a guard.
- Streaming through the models proxy (raw SSE probes): text and `reasoning_content` arrive token by token (gaps
  under 1.5 s), but tool-call arguments are held back until complete (a 60-row output tool: first argument byte at
  64 s, all at once); quiet stretches carry `: keepalive` comments every 10 s. Headers come with the first (role)
  chunk: within 9.4 s in 179 of 180 calls (p90 5.9 s, either mode). The one hang (thinking off) sent no headers
  and nothing else for 200 s, so "no first chunk in 20 s" catches it; a tool call's silence cannot be told from a
  stall, so tool requests keep their per-mode timeout as allowed silence.
- `LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1` A/B (30 agent calls each, run side by side): excluding one prompt that sends thinking-on
  reasoning into minutes, median 13.2 s vs 14.4 s, p90 74 vs 81 s, max 89 vs 268 s (deadline retried a legit
  thinking-on long answer twice); 2 no-first-chunk retries caught at 20 s. On the runaway-reasoning prompt the
  deadline failed 2 of 8 after 6 retries x 90 s, the watchdog finished 8 of 8 but took 87 to 811 s (6 calls hit
  the 300 s cap). Progress does not end runaway reasoning: keep the cap lower (LLM_MAX_CALL 120 to 150) or cap
  output tokens before turning the watchdog on.
- v2 orchestrator local runs (planner -> board -> workers -> verify -> calc): the planner picked all four fact kinds
  and mapped each to the right site from the brief alone (23 s); the tender worker resolved 5 positions with final
  quantities and keys in 75 to 105 s; the mail plan named 9 record kinds. `Trace.event()` takes `kind` and `worker`
  positionally, so board events must not pass keywords of those names (two runs lost every posted fact to that).
- The spec worker (`research.py`, thinking off) twice looped between two controls on one page for its full 25
  steps and found no revision history, so no requirement reached the ERP; it needs a loop guard or thinking on
  for that step. Mail kinds that find nothing burn the full 20-step budget (about 70 s per kind and tab).
- A thinking verifier call over a batch of facts can outlast a 120 s budget; verify runs thinking off with the
  long-timeout reader model by default.
- v2 end to end, local (planner -> board -> tender, spec + ERP, mail -> verify -> calc): one run reached the full
  answer (local check 100/100) in 752 s of research; other runs lost the spec (navigator paged between two list
  pages for 25 steps, or clicked row menus the popup closer shut), the mail tabs (sign-ins hung or landed on the
  browser error page) or the ERP (a look() wrapper missing the new keywords). Each now has a guard: a loop hint
  after three arrivals on one page, one thinking retry for the spec, time-limited starts with a retry that also
  rejects error pages, staggered mail tabs that join when ready, and a mail deadline with partial results.
- Mail records only count with the bidder's domain: when the address lookup ran on a tab that showed an error
  page, every authority record was dropped silently. The address now comes from the first tab that shows it.
- A requirement whose stroke reserve was not found came back without a material and calc turned the whole bid
  into no_bid. Undecided materials (pending inputs, search problems) now omit the position; only a complete
  search without a match means no_bid.
- One run with the mail kinds on site_tools.search/collect kept nothing in three kinds (150 s each; paging
  followed a message list into a session expiry); kept on the paging tool for now.
- First v2 sandbox test run (orchestrator branch 405b1f4): quality 100, eligible, about 10 min, 308 model calls,
  $0.134. The full pipeline works in the sandbox; the variance across repeats decides what to submit.
- v2 round 1 (4 sandbox test runs of 405b1f4): 100 (10 min), 100 with the watchdog (15 min), 10 (spec navigator
  found no revision history, so every position was omitted and the found discount was lost too), and NO BID: a false
  summary-check alarm switched signing to thinking, the model went back in the wizard (clears later steps) and the
  deadline cut it before the TAN was entered. Signing needs its own time reserve and must never go back.
- sub_9bd976b00673121a (quality 100, 14:02, rank #2) was the watchdog test run promoted to a submission from its run
  page. Its exact code is branch submitted/sub_9bd976b0. It still has the old signing weakness (no bid when signing
  overruns), so replace it once the fixed version scores 100 reliably across several test runs.
- Soak run 1 (3f5d6b6): NO BID. The sites were slow (several tabs hit the 45 s settle cap at once), the webmail
  session failed both starts and lost its tab, and submit_bid's address lookup then crashed on the empty tab list
  (IndexError), which ended solve() before signing. Fixed: sessions reopen a lost tab, mail lookups never raise,
  solve() retries signing once after an unexpected error.

Usage: atira logs <run> [--follow]

Print a test or scored run's logs; --follow polls until the run has ended
101:| `test-run <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset and open its run page; `--follow` prints its place in the queue, then streams its logs here |
106:| `logs <run> [--follow]` | A test or scored run's logs; `--follow` keeps polling until the run has ended |
109:| `mcp` | Serve MCP on stdio for your coding agent: list and debug runs (why one failed, logs by time, model calls, where the time went, a browser's screen at a time, recorded inputs, two runs compared), start and wait for test runs, and cancel a run or submit when you confirm ([MCP guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)) |
181:atira test-run ./my-agent --follow    # the same, and its logs here until it ends
188:the browser: the browser, the logs, the phases and the score with its full breakdown, live. `submit` opens your team
194:`test-run --follow` then streams the run's logs as `logs --follow` does and exits 7 if the run failed or timed out.
222:`logs <run>` prints what the run has written so far; `--follow` polls with a growing pause (1 s, up to 10 s) and
233:| `ATIRA_POLL_MS` | The first pause of `logs --follow`, in milliseconds (default 1000) |
250:| 7 | `logs --follow` or `test-run --follow`: the run failed or timed out; `submit --follow`: the submission did not complete |

content.content:
# Debug runs from your coding agent

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

`atira mcp` makes the CLI an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents can read your runs
and debug them with you: find the failing step in the logs, see the browser's screen at that moment, check what the
agent clicked and typed, then start the next test run. It uses the CLI's sign-in, so there is nothing new to set up.

## Set it up

Install the CLI and sign in once ([CLI guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)):

```sh
curl -fsSL $API/install.sh | sh
atira login
```

Then add the server to your coding agent:

```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # Claude Code
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp      # Codex
```

Other clients (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, ...) take the usual `mcpServers` entry:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "atira": { "command": "atira", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

For Codex you can also write it in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.atira]
command = "atira"
args = ["mcp"]
```

If your editor can't find `atira`, give its full path: `command -v atira` prints it. `ATIRA_TOKEN` works instead of
the stored sign-in, and `atira mcp --help` prints these lines.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | About |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `challenge_brief` | The challenge: task, websites, rules and limits, run contract, scoring and answer schema | 6k tokens |
| `list_runs` | Your team's recent test and scored runs: status, quality, cost, time and package | 50 tokens a run |
| `get_run` | One run: status and failure, queue place or warm-up while it waits, phases, package, model calls by model with failures and queue waits, points per field, recordings, answer, run page | 1–2k |
| `diagnose_run` | Why a run failed and whether to rerun it as it is: the failure class, the last 20 stdout and stderr lines, model errors, idle stretches over 60 s, browsers whose screen froze | 2–3k |
| `run_logs` | Log lines in time order, by time (`from`, `to`), stream, text (`grep`) and `browser`; `tail` for the last lines; page by page | 30 a line |
| `run_llm_calls` | Every model call, one line each, under a header with time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and, for models the organizers host, the queue wait | 35 a call |
| `run_profile` | Where the time went, per 30 s, 1 min or 5 min: inputs and screen activity per browser, model calls, seconds and cost; then the critical path | 1.5–3k |
| `run_screenshot` | A browser's screen at a time with the clicks just before it marked, every browser at once (`browser: "all"`), or a filmstrip (`frames`) | 1.5k an image |
| `run_inputs` | The clicks, scrolls and typing the platform recorded in each browser, with their times | 25 an input |
| `compare_runs` | Two runs side by side: package, quality, time, cost, cost × time, calls and failures per model, phases, points per field and answer fields that changed | 1–2k |
| `wait_for_run` | Wait until a run is running or done, including recording collection and scoring (at most `timeout_s`, default 50 s), then say how it stands | 300 |
| `list_submissions` | Your scored submissions: review status, any organizer note, result and package | 60 a submission |
| `get_submission` | One submission (`sub_...`): review status, any organizer note, its runs | 300–800 |
| `run_package` | The package a run or submission used, as uploaded: SHA-256, label, agent.json and each file's size, never the contents; `out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder | 15 a file |
| `leaderboard` | The board with each entry's cost × time and the Pareto front, your rank and the gap to the next; `compare_run` places one of your runs on it | 500 |
| `models` | The models the organizers host, if any, and how to call them from your computer through `atira models proxy` | 300 |
| `test_run` | Pack a folder and start a test run; returns its id, queue place, package SHA-256 and label (the git commit by default) | 150 |
| `cancel_run` | Cancel one of your runs that hasn't finished; only with `confirm: true` | 60 |
| `submit` | Pack a folder and submit it for a scored run, public and final; only with `confirm: true` after the person said yes | 100 |

Everything only reads, except `test_run`, `cancel_run` and `submit`, and `run_package` with `out`, which saves a file on your computer. A scored submission is public and can't be undone, and a cancelled run
doesn't come back, so `submit` and `cancel_run` refuse unless the call says `confirm: true`: tell your agent to ask
you first. Your agent sees only what your team sees on the run page; another team's run is "404: run not found".

Run tools take a run id (`run_...`), a test run id (`reh_...`) or a submission id (`sub_...`, meaning its latest run).
`run_package` takes the same ids; a submission id there means the package it submitted, which its runs ran.

## What it shows

`get_run` while a run waits, then once it failed:

```
run_8af0981b3710558a · test run on the public dataset · package 3f2a1c9e0b12 (2 files) "a41c2d9-dirty"
Status queued, phase queued
Queued: 2 runs ahead of yours, starts in about 3 min
...
Status failed, phase done · Failure: Run exited with code 0 without submitting an answer (no answer)
```

`run_llm_calls`:

```
run_0d7f1203b576189a · 86 model calls in a run of 16:22 · $0.4130
Time in calls 6:41 · latency p50 2.1s, p95 31s · at most 4 at once (at 02:13)
  anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5: 33 calls, $0.4126, 57,619 in (72,128 cached) / 5,867 out, 2:05 in calls
  openai/gpt-5-mini: 1 call, $0.0004, 1,845 in / 12 out, 1.2s in calls
Failures: openai: 52 failed (429 rate limited)

[02:10.4 +3.2s] anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 200 in 4,210 (cached 3,900) out 312 $0.00471 id=c_812
[02:13.9 +0.4s] openai 429 rate limited $0.00 id=c_815
```

`run_profile` (the screen columns are seconds the browser's screen was changing; `–` is still):

```
time   b1 in · screen  b2 in · screen  b3 in · screen  b4 in · screen  calls  in calls  busy  cost
02:00  6 · 21s         3 · 8.0s        10 · 44s        0 · –           14     1:02      48s   $0.0612
03:00  4 · 12s         0 · –           0 · –           2 · 3.5s        3      41s       38s   $0.0140
Critical path:
Longest stretches over 10 s with no input, no screen change and no model call in flight:
  03:12.4–04:40.1 (01:27)
    last line before: [03:11.9] stdout: mail TAN: waiting for the TAN message
Browsers that went quiet:
  browser 3: last screen change at 02:45.4, then nothing for 04:53 until the end
```

`diagnose_run` names the failure's class and the next step: `cancelled`, `no answer` (your agent system ended
without entering one: fix it, a rerun alone won't help), `agent exit` (see stderr), `timeout` (make it faster),
`answer rejected` (fix the answer's shape) or `platform` (not your agent system: rerun it as it is). A reason that
starts with "Setup" is agent.json's setup: `run_logs` with stream `setup` shows why. Where the platform records a
run's failure class, that one is used.

## Times

Times are on the run's clock, as the run page shows them: `02:13`, `1:02:13`, `3m20s` or `133` seconds from the
run's start, or an ISO 8601 time; durations are written the same way. The same time in the run page's address,
`?t=02:13`, opens the replay there. Links point at the platform's own address, whichever name the CLI talks to.

A screenshot is cut from the recording with ffmpeg on the platform. If the platform can't do that right now, the
CLI cuts it with your own ffmpeg (`brew install ffmpeg`, or `sudo apt install ffmpeg`); without one it says so and
links the replay. A time outside a recording gets its nearest frame and says so ("browser 1's recording covers
-00:03.7–07:48.9").

## What it can't do

- **Past frames of a live run.** The recording is stored after the run ends and collection finishes; until then `run_screenshot` shows each
  browser's latest live frame, about a second behind the screen (its time says when), and
  filmstrips and screen activity wait for the end. The run page's live view shows it moving.
- **Logs as they arrive.** Tools answer once; `wait_for_run` waits up to 600 s if your client allows long tool calls
  (Codex stops a tool after 60 s unless you raise `tool_timeout_sec`). In a terminal, `atira logs <run> --follow`
  streams a run's logs until it ends.
- **Log streams** are `setup`, `stdout`, `stderr` and `input`: errors are in `stderr` and in `get_run`/`diagnose_run`,
  screen activity is in `run_profile`.
- **Typed secrets.** Inputs show typed text with keys, tokens and your run's secrets masked.

From a terminal, `atira cancel <run>` cancels a run and `atira status` lists your submissions and test runs.

## Try it

Ask your agent things like:

- "Why did my last test run fail? Diagnose it, then show me the screen at the moment it went idle."
- "Where did the time go in run_19932ad4ade523e4? Which model calls were slowest?"
- "Compare my last two test runs: what changed in the score and the cost?"
- "Start a test run of ./my-agent, wait until it's running, and show me every browser's screen at 01:00."

| `run_inputs` | The clicks, scrolls and typing the platform recorded in each browser, with their times | 25 an input |
| `compare_runs` | Two runs side by side: package, quality, time, cost, cost × time, calls and failures per model, phases, points per field and answer fields that changed | 1–2k |
| `wait_for_run` | Wait until a run is running or done, including recording collection and scoring (at most `timeout_s`, default 50 s), then say how it stands | 300 |
| `list_submissions` | Your scored submissions: review status, any organizer note, result and package | 60 a submission |
| `get_submission` | One submission (`sub_...`): review status, any organizer note, its runs | 300–800 |
| `run_package` | The package a run or submission used, as uploaded: SHA-256, label, agent.json and each file's size, never the contents; `out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder | 15 a file |
| `leaderboard` | The board with each entry's cost × time and the Pareto front, your rank and the gap to the next; `compare_run` places one of your runs on it | 500 |
| `models` | The models the organizers host, if any, and how to call them from your computer through `atira models proxy` | 300 |
| `test_run` | Pack a folder and start a test run; returns its id, queue place, package SHA-256 and label (the git commit by default) | 150 |
| `cancel_run` | Cancel one of your runs that hasn't finished; only with `confirm: true` | 60 |
| `submit` | Pack a folder and submit it for a scored run, public and final; only with `confirm: true` after the person said yes | 100 |

Everything only reads, except `test_run`, `cancel_run` and `submit`, and `run_package` with `out`, which saves a file on your computer. A scored submission is public and can't be undone, and a cancelled run
doesn't come back, so `submit` and `cancel_run` refuse unless the call says `confirm: true`: tell your agent to ask
you first. Your agent sees only what your team sees on the run page; another team's run is "404: run not found".

Run tools take a run id (`run_...`), a test run id (`reh_...`) or a submission id (`sub_...`, meaning its latest run).
`run_package` takes the same ids; a submission id there means the package it submitted, which its runs ran.

## What it shows

`get_run` while a run waits, then once it failed:

```
run_8af0981b3710558a · test run on the public dataset · package 3f2a1c9e0b12 (2 files) "a41c2d9-dirty"
Status queued, phase queued
Queued: 2 runs ahead of yours, starts in about 3 min
...
Status failed, phase done · Failure: Run exited with code 0 without submitting an answer (no answer)
```

`run_llm_calls`:

```
run_0d7f1203b576189a · 86 model calls in a run of 16:22 · $0.4130
Time in calls 6:41 · latency p50 2.1s, p95 31s · at most 4 at once (at 02:13)
  anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5: 33 calls, $0.4126, 57,619 in (72,128 cached) / 5,867 out, 2:05 in calls
  openai/gpt-5-mini: 1 call, $0.0004, 1,845 in / 12 out, 1.2s in calls
Failures: openai: 52 failed (429 rate limited)

[02:10.4 +3.2s] anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 200 in 4,210 (cached 3,900) out 312 $0.00471 id=c_812
[02:13.9 +0.4s] openai 429 rate limited $0.00 id=c_815
```

`run_profile` (the screen columns are seconds the browser's screen was changing; `–` is still):

```
time   b1 in · screen  b2 in · screen  b3 in · screen  b4 in · screen  calls  in calls  busy  cost
02:00  6 · 21s         3 · 8.0s        10 · 44s        0 · –           14     1:02      48s   $0.0612
03:00  4 · 12s         0 · –           0 · –           2 · 3.5s        3      41s       38s   $0.0140
Critical path:
Longest stretches over 10 s with no input, no screen change and no model call in flight:
  03:12.4–04:40.1 (01:27)
    last line before: [03:11.9] stdout: mail TAN: waiting for the TAN message
Browsers that went quiet:
  browser 3: last screen change at 02:45.4, then nothing for 04:53 until the end
```

`diagnose_run` names the failure's class and the next step: `cancelled`, `no answer` (your agent system ended
without entering one: fix it, a rerun alone won't help), `agent exit` (see stderr), `timeout` (make it faster),
`answer rejected` (fix the answer's shape) or `platform` (not your agent system: rerun it as it is). A reason that
starts with "Setup" is agent.json's setup: `run_logs` with stream `setup` shows why. Where the platform records a
run's failure class, that one is used.

## Times

Times are on the run's clock, as the run page shows them: `02:13`, `1:02:13`, `3m20s` or `133` seconds from the
run's start, or an ISO 8601 time; durations are written the same way. The same time in the run page's address,
`?t=02:13`, opens the replay there. Links point at the platform's own address, whichever name the CLI talks to.

A screenshot is cut from the recording with ffmpeg on the platform. If the platform can't do that right now, the
CLI cuts it with your own ffmpeg (`brew install ffmpeg`, or `sudo apt install ffmpeg`); without one it says so and
links the replay. A time outside a recording gets its nearest frame and says so ("browser 1's recording covers
-00:03.7–07:48.9").

## What it can't do

- **Past frames of a live run.** The recording is stored after the run ends and collection finishes; until then `run_screenshot` shows each
  browser's latest live frame, about a second behind the screen (its time says when), and
  filmstrips and screen activity wait for the end. The run page's live view shows it moving.
- **Logs as they arrive.** Tools answer once; `wait_for_run` waits up to 600 s if your client allows long tool calls
  (Codex stops a tool after 60 s unless you raise `tool_timeout_sec`). In a terminal, `atira logs <run> --follow`
  streams a run's logs until it ends.
- **Log streams** are `setup`, `stdout`, `stderr` and `input`: errors are in `stderr` and in `get_run`/`diagnose_run`,
  screen activity is in `run_profile`.
- **Typed secrets.** Inputs show typed text with keys, tokens and your run's secrets masked.

From a terminal, `atira cancel <run>` cancels a run and `atira status` lists your submissions and test runs.

## Try it

Ask your agent things like:

- "Why did my last test run fail? Diagnose it, then show me the screen at the moment it went idle."
- "Where did the time go in run_19932ad4ade523e4? Which model calls were slowest?"
- "Compare my last two test runs: what changed in the score and the cost?"
- "Start a test run of ./my-agent, wait until it's running, and show me every browser's screen at 01:00."

#!/bin/sh
# Start a sandbox test run of agent/ (public data, never ranked), follow it to the end and record its score in
# experiments/runs.jsonl (commit that file afterwards). Usage, from anywhere: dev/test-run.sh <version> ["note"] [experiment]
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/test-run.sh <version> [note] [experiment]}
note=${2:-}
experiment=${3:-}
commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
dirty=no; [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- agent)" ] && dirty=yes
log=$(mktemp)
record="python3 dev/track.py platform RUN --version '$version' --experiment '$experiment' --note '$note' --commit $commit --dirty $dirty"
trap 'run=$(grep -o "run_[0-9a-f]*" "$log" | head -1); echo; echo "Stopped following; the run goes on. Record it once it ends:"; echo "  $record" | sed "s/RUN/${run:-<run id>}/"; exit 130' INT
atira test-run ./agent --no-open --follow </dev/null | tee "$log"
run=$(grep -o 'run_[0-9a-f]*' "$log" | head -1)
rm -f "$log"
[ -n "$run" ] || { echo "No run id in the output; record it later with: $record"; exit 1; }
eval "$(echo "$record" | sed "s/RUN/$run/")" && python3 dev/track.py report
dev/:
clef_eval
configurator_check.py
research_check_records.py
research_check.py
robustness.py
run-local.sh
site_tools_check.py
smoke.py
soak.py

track.py

content.content:
**How do my teammates and I sign in from a terminal?** Each person runs `atira login` on their own computer
and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.
Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code to approve elsewhere.

**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
tokens' access to it at once.

**My invite link says it is for someone else.** Invites are for one GitHub account. Sign in with the account
the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.
## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
  - Cache writes: Free
  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
```

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
  - Output: Not priced

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

27	# Closes modal <dialog>s and aria-modal popups through their own close button as soon as they open, and records
28	# what it closed. Links inside popups ("accept and continue") are never followed.
29	AUTO_CLOSE_JS = r"""
30	(() => {
31	  if (window.__arInit) return;
32	  window.__arInit = true;
33	  const CLOSE = /^(×|✕|✖|x|schließen|schliessen|close|dismiss|ausblenden|später|later|nicht jetzt|not now)$/i;
34	  const closed = (window.__arClosed = window.__arClosed || []);
35	  function closeButton(d) {
36	    for (const b of d.querySelectorAll('button,[role=button]')) {
37	      const name = (b.getAttribute('aria-label') || b.textContent || '').trim();
38	      if (CLOSE.test(name) || b.hasAttribute('data-close')) return b;
39	    }
40	    return null;
41	  }
42	  function check() {
43	    for (const d of document.querySelectorAll('dialog[open],[role=dialog][aria-modal=true],[role=alertdialog]')) {
44	      const modal = d.tagName !== 'DIALOG' || d.matches(':modal');
45	      if (!modal || d.dataset.arClosed) continue;
46	      const b = closeButton(d);
47	      if (!b) continue;
48	      d.dataset.arClosed = '1';
49	      closed.push((d.getAttribute('aria-label') || d.querySelector('h1,h2,h3')?.textContent || 'popup').trim());
50	      b.click();
51	      if (d.tagName === 'DIALOG' && d.open) d.close();
52	    }
53	  }
54	  const start = () => {
55	    check();
56	    new MutationObserver(check).observe(document.documentElement,
57	      {subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open', 'aria-modal', 'style', 'class']});
58	  };
59	  if (document.documentElement) start(); else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', start);
60	})();

68	  const labels = e => e.labels ? Array.from(e.labels).map(l => l.textContent) : [];

72	    const around = text(r) + ' ' + (r.parentElement ? r.parentElement.textContent : '');
73	    const max = r.max || '100';

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

Priority answer (sites never opened): the site was very slow but still alive, and our start sequence threw away each attempt that was making progress.

Evidence (a27e, 9371, 487200 all show the same pattern; no recordings exist, so this is from traces and platform inputs):
- Each attempt is goto (30 s domcontentloaded cap), then settle (45 s cap), then look(), all inside START_SECONDS=90. The first settle timeout always lands at exactly 75.2 s (30+45), and start_failed fires at 90.0 / 180.0 / 270 / 360. So the navigation never fired domcontentloaded within 30 s, and no helper (login, cookies, human_check) found anything for 45 s.
- On attempt 1 browser 1 (tender) records ZERO inputs, so the login form never rendered. The page was not a chrome-error page: no ConnectionError and no reload of an error page; the errors are bare TimeoutError.
- The sites were intermittently alive. In 487200 the tender login page did render on attempt 2 after 5.8 s (login typed at 95.8 s), but the post-login page then hung: settle timed out at 135 s and look() timed out at 180 s. In a27e the tender login rendered on the 5th attempt (372.7 s) and the post-login page hung again (settle timeouts at 412 and 532 s, start_failed at 457 and 547 s).
- In 487200 the tender portal (browser 1) and ERP (browser 3) failed in lockstep with identical timestamps (75.2 / 90.0 / 180.0 / 504 / 594 s), while the customer portal and webmail in browsers 2 and 4 worked. Two different browsers stalling together points at the server side of those two sites, not one broken browser or our event loop. a27e had the loop watchdog and it never dumped.
- In other runs the same sites showed 'Locator.evaluate: Timeout 30000ms' on clicks (f93e, 164e, 3d85). That means the page's renderer or backend was stalling mid-run too.
- Collateral damage: the briefing waits for every start to finish (180 s) and the planner waits for a second pair of attempts (another 180 s). That is 360 s with nothing running (platform profile: 05:54 idle, 00:08 to 06:03, in a27e and 9371). Then an IndexError in look() on the tab-less session killed both a27e and 9371 (exit 1, 0 points; fixed later with revive).
- ERP alone failed to start in f93e (276 and 366 s), and all 5 positions were lost.

What would work better:
1) Never close a tab that is still loading. One attempt should keep waiting on the same tab with a longer cap (about 180 to 240 s). Today each retry throws away a navigation or login that was halfway through.
2) Keep retrying in the background with backoff (for example 30, 60, 120 s) until a hard deadline about 300 s before the end, instead of 2 attempts. Only the bid site truly gates points: a signed bid with no positions is worth 10, versus 0 without one.
3) Decouple the briefing and planner from site starts. The brief does not need the tender portal; start research on the sites that are up, and let the bid-site session keep warming in parallel. Starting the bid site first and keeping it warm is good, but it must not block anything.
4) A fresh browser context per attempt is unlikely to help, because two browsers failed in lockstep. A cheap way to rule it out is one attempt in a new context after two failures.
5) Make the start budget phase-aware: goto 60 s, then settle as long as the start budget allows, rather than fixed 30+45 inside 90.

Two different browsers stalling together points at the server side of those two sites, not one broken browser or our event loop. a27e had the loop watchdog and it never dumped.
- In other runs the same sites showed 'Locator.evaluate: Timeout 30000ms' on clicks (f93e, 164e, 3d85). That means the page's renderer or backend was stalling mid-run too.
- Collateral damage: the briefing waits for every start to finish (180 s) and the planner waits for a second pair of attempts (another 180 s). That is 360 s with nothing running (platform profile: 05:54 idle, 00:08 to 06:03, in a27e and 9371). Then an IndexError in look() on the tab-less session killed both a27e and 9371 (exit 1, 0 points; fixed later with revive).
- ERP alone failed to start in f93e (276 and 366 s), and all 5 positions were lost.

What would work better:
1) Never close a tab that is still loading. One attempt should keep waiting on the same tab with a longer cap (about 180 to 240 s). Today each retry throws away a navigation or login that was halfway through.
2) Keep retrying in the background with backoff (for example 30, 60, 120 s) until a hard deadline about 300 s before the end, instead of 2 attempts. Only the bid site truly gates points: a signed bid with no positions is worth 10, versus 0 without one.
3) Decouple the briefing and planner from site starts. The brief does not need the tender portal; start research on the sites that are up, and let the bid-site session keep warming in parallel. Starting the bid site first and keeping it warm is good, but it must not block anything.
4) A fresh browser context per attempt is unlikely to help, because two browsers failed in lockstep. A cheap way to rule it out is one attempt in a new context after two failures.
5) Make the start budget phase-aware: goto 60 s, then settle as long as the start budget allows, rather than fixed 30+45 inside 90.

# v2 sandbox runs since 19:20 UTC: why 100 sometimes and not other times

Read-only analysis; nothing was edited, started or committed.

## Data and its limits

- Sources: `atira status --json`, `atira logs`, and the platform MCP (`atira mcp`: run_llm_calls, run_profile,
  get_run, run_logs). Raw files are in `tmp/logs/` (`<run>.log`, `.llm.txt`, `.profile.txt`, `.get.txt`) and
  `tmp/status/`.
- **The platform keeps only the last ~260 stdout lines per run.** run_logs reports "263 of 263 matching lines" for
  every run, and the earliest trace line kept falls between 160 s and 500 s. Briefing, planner and the first
  spec, tender and ERP minutes are therefore lost, except in a27e, 487200 and 49b0 (short or failing runs whose
  starts survived). Phase starts below are back-computed from `seconds=` on done/stopped/spec_done/tender_facts
  lines. Model calls (run_llm_calls) and inputs per browser are complete. No run has a screen recording.
- Fix for the future: write the full trace to a file and print a 30-line phase summary at the end, or log fewer
  helper lines. Otherwise the platform keeps only the last ~260 lines.
- run_d4deebd2d3a2d429 (19:31, quality 10) ran package 5699c0ad (the v1 submission), so it is not v2 and is
  excluded. Runs started after about 21:40 (c5b0, 7d02, 1fa4, 3e4f, cc0d, e4e1, ...) were still running or
  unrecorded and are not covered.

## 1. Per run

Score fields: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total_net 5, total_consistency 5, withdrawn_answer 5,
index_window 5, positions 5 x 13. Every 100 run scored full points on every field. Every 10 run scored only
decision + reference (with no positions, discount, totals, withdrawn and index score 0 as well).

| run (package) | q | orch. start | research end | form | sign | end | first failure that cost points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 06a3 (405b1f4) | 100 | 8 | 371 | 373-559 (185 s, 4 output_refused) | 560-591 | 591 | none |
| 715a scored (405b1f4+wd) | 100 | 9 | 527 | 529-665 | 667-840 (first TAN lookup returned the reference, 2nd took 125 s) | 840 | none (signing ~5 min before the 1110 s end) |
| 8e5c (spec-redundancy 3c7d25c) | 100 | 9 | 586 | 588-720 | 723-748 | 748 | none |
| 4b941 (spec-redundancy 421072d) | 100 | 5 | 621 | 624-781 | 784-813 | 813 | none (research ended 9 s before the 630 s deadline) |
| df14 (405b1f4) | 10 | 54 | 620 | 622-675 | 677-793 | 793 | spec: no revision history, both attempts (spec2 hit 25 steps at 346 s) |
| f910 (405b1f4) | 0 | 9 | 594 | 595-765 | 767-1110 timeout | - | spec read only A-5 (4 of 5 positions omitted); then a false summary_check alarm, thinking signing went back in the wizard, out of time |
| 817c (0103702) | 10 | 55 | 727 | 730-827 | 828-856 | 856 | tender worker stopped at the 630 s research deadline, so no positions; end_reserves kept 4 records, A-2 stroke 507 vs 500 |
| 9371 (3f5d6b6) | 0 | 360 | 635 | - | - | crash | tender portal never opened (4 x 90 s at start, again at 551 s); IndexError in look() |
| f93e (ade4) | 0 | 180 | 663 | 665-870 stuck | - | hung, cancelled | ERP start failed twice (276, 366 s), so no ERP data; form phase settle timeout and hang |
| 6a01 (3f5d6b6) | 0 | ? | >549 | - | - | hung, cancelled | spec took 268 s (done 466 s); ERP worker hit step limit 12; process hung after 549 s |
| 3004 (b8220fb) | 0 | 7 | 599 (full 5-position answer) | 602-684 | 689-1110 timeout | - | false summary_check alarm ("position table omits per-piece amounts"), thinking signing, timeout |
| 164e (b8220fb) | 0 | ? | ~600 | ~684-1110 | - | cancelled | form click hung (Locator.evaluate 30 s timeout at 765 s), form step stuck 426 s |
| a27e (630849a) | 0 | 360 | 630 | - | - | crash | tender portal never opened; IndexError |
| 3d85 (b8f76fa) | 10 | 7 | 767 | 783-946 timeout | 946-1058 | 1058 | spec attempt 1 looped 25 steps (160 s); spec2 needed 248 s for the revision history, so the requirements were opened at 629 s and hit the 630 s deadline |
| 49b0 (b8f76fa) | 10 | 180 | 591 | 594-658 | 661-696 | 696 | customer portal (spec) never opened, 2 attempts by 368 s |
| 487200 (e6f5216) | 0 | 414 (plan) | 594+ | - | - | no answer | tender portal and ERP never opened (failed in lockstep at 75/90/180/504/594 s) |

Times are seconds on the run clock. "orch. start" is orchestrator done minus its `seconds=`, i.e. when research
began (planner included). Spec, tender and ERP starts are mostly not in the kept logs. Where seen: spec start
~178-199 s in 6a01 and f93e, tender_facts 257-321 s (done at 310-444 s), ERP material reads 270-520 s.

## 2. Model calls and site slowness

| run | calls | p50 | p90 | max | >45 s | errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 06a3 | 308 | 3.1 | 12 | 45 | 0 | 0 |
| 715a | 285 | 2.8 | 11 | 41 | 0 | 0 |
| 8e5c | 389 | 3.6 | 14 | 59 | 3 | 0 |
| 4b941 | 434 | 3.0 | 11 | 47 | 1 | 0 |
| df14 | 189 | 2.8 | 13 | 36 | 0 | 0 |
| f910 | 231 | 2.8 | 13 | 32 | 0 | 0 |
| 817c | 308 | 2.7 | 12 | 33 | 0 | 0 |
| 9371 | 169 | 2.4 | 8 | 20 | 0 | 0 |
| f93e | 120 | 4.0 | 15 | 33 | 0 | 0 |
| 6a01 | 239 | 2.6 | 10 | 33 | 0 | 0 |
| 3004 | 292 | 3.3 | 10 | 38 | 0 | 0 |
| 164e | 288 | 3.7 | 14 | 58 | 1 | 0 |
| a27e | 75 | 2.5 | 9 | 19 | 0 | 0 |

- Platform-side failures: none. The only non-200s are the expected 401s after the bid is in.
- Concurrency: at most 9 to 17 calls at once per run. Team-wide calls in flight (all runs overlaid) peaked at 20,
  under the 32-per-team cap.
- Queue wait: test runs show 63-92 % of call time as "queue wait"; the scored run 715a shows 7 % (p50 0.3 s). The
  total latency is the same in both, so this is how the platform accounts for time, not extra delay.
- **Model latency does not separate the 100 runs from the failures.**
- Site slowness signals:

| run | settle timeouts | start_failed | click/evaluate 30 s timeouts | step-limit stops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a27e | 6 | 6 | 0 | 1 |
| 487200 | 6+ | 8 | 0 | - |
| 9371 | 3 (+4 inferred) | 3 (+4) | 0 | 0 |
| f93e | 2 | 2 | 3 | 0 |
| 49b0 | - | 2 | - | - |
| f910 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 164e | 0 | 0 | 1 (hung 345 s) | 4 |
| 3d85 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| 100 runs | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0-1 |

- Mail stops at the 150 s cap per kind: 2-10 per run, including the 100 runs.
- Mail kind wall time (all runs): mean 103-158 s, max 259-344 s. Kinds left empty: commitments 2/12,
  approval 2/7, packaging 2/8, project_bonus 2/7.

## 3. Failure taxonomy (points lost x frequency, 16 runs, 1,250 points lost)

1. **A site that will not open or stalls** (tender, ERP or customer portal start fails, or a page hangs a click
   or settle for minutes): 9371, a27e, 487200, f93e, 49b0, 164e, 6a01. 7 runs, ~690 points.
   - A failing start blocks the briefing for 180 s and the planner for another 180 s.
   - A failing bid site leaves no way to sign: 0 instead of 10.
2. **Spec navigation** (revision history not found within 25 steps, or found too late): df14, 3d85, f910.
   3 runs, ~270 points.
3. **False summary_check alarm, after which signing goes back and times out**: f910, 3004. 2 runs, 200 points;
   3004 had a full answer.
4. **Research deadline cuts a slow worker** (tender facts by 630 s): 817c. 1 run, 90 points.
   - The same deadline nearly cut 4b941 (research ended at 621 s).

Critical path in the 100 runs:
- Research (start to orchestrator done) took 363-615 s. The last inputs were the mail kinds (end_reserves and
  condition_rules done at 539-570 s in 8e5c and 4b941; project_bonus at 476 s in 715a), then verify (17-45 s).
- A-2 and A-4 ("stroke pending") always wait for the end_reserves mail, so mail is on the critical path for 3 of
  the 5 positions.
- Form took 132-185 s and signing 25-30 s (173 s when the first TAN lookup was wrong).
- What the 100 runs had that the failing runs lacked:
  - every site opened at first try;
  - the spec found the current revision on the first attempt (or the parallel spec attempts did, in 8e5c and
    4b941);
  - the tender facts were in before ~450 s;
  - summary_check matched, so signing stayed on the thinking-off path.
- Their timings were not faster than some failures: 4b941 finished research only 9 s before the deadline.

## 4. Recommendations

1. **Start the bid site in the background and never block on it.** Keep the tab when an attempt times out; wait
   up to ~240 s on that same tab, then retry with backoff (30/60/120 s) until about end-300 s.
   - Run the briefing and planner from the brief and the sites that are up.
   - Saves 180-360 s in 5 runs, and turns 3 zeros into at least 10.
   - Do the same for the ERP and the customer portal. A site lost late should still allow a signed partial bid.
2. **Never let summary_check switch signing to thinking or go back.** A mismatch should be logged and the bid
   signed as entered; at most allow one thinking-off fix on the review page without a back button.
   - +200 points in 2 of 16 runs.
3. **Spec redundancy from t=0** (what 8e5c and 4b941 ran): two parallel spec attempts with different
   strategies, each capped at ~150 s / 25 steps, and a third if neither has a revision by 300 s.
   - The spec must be done by ~350 s, so the ERP (100-130 s) and verify (cap 45 s; 3d85 spent 137 s) fit before
     the deadline.
4. **Move the research deadline from 630 s to ~720 s, and make the end-phase budgets explicit.**
   - Form: 200 s budget (observed max 185 s), plus a 30 s bound per click.
   - Signing: 180 s reserve (observed 25-173 s).
   - last_chance at end-120 s.
   - With 1110 s as the end, research can run to 1110-200-180 = 730 s. That would have saved 817c (tender at
     630 s) and likely 3d85 (requirements opened at 629 s).
5. **Step limits:**
   - ERP material views: 12 is hit in 5 runs (once 14); raise to 16-18 or scale with time left (as 3d6edf8 does).
   - Spec: 25 steps is enough when the navigator does not loop; keep 25 plus a loop guard, rather than raising
     it.
   - Mail: 150 s per kind is too low for 4 of the 9 kinds at p90; give end_reserves and condition_rules (critical
     path) 200 s and start them first; give the others 150 s.
6. **Parallelism pays most on the spec and on starting the critical mail kinds first.** It does not pay on model
   calls (no queue pressure: 20 calls in flight team-wide at peak).
7. Keep the full trace beyond the platform's ~260-line tail (see "Data and its limits").
